gaps.q: UI evidence for 'real backend' rests on the 404 notice plus the trace network log (browser → http://127.0.0.1:8006, Origin :5180); the two UI tests do not assert the response status or the body detail 'dev routes disabled' in-browser. Claimed failure mode: a route-not-found 404 from an unrelated cause would render the same notice and pass the same assertions.

On #a1-workbench the dev-routes note co-occurs with a governance 502 (files/tree). The gating is isCoordinatorNotFound (status===404) in code and the same page load shows /api/dev/test-data-projects → 404 in the trace, but no browser run isolates the two (e.g. dev routes enabled + governance 502 → note must be absent). Claimed failure mode: note shown for a non-404 failure would be a false 'dev routes closed' message; only vitest covers that branch.

The Edge Console shell header renders static text 'COORDINATOR 8004' / 'COORD :8004' (EdgeConsole.tsx:355/358) while every request in this run went to :8006. Pre-existing and outside this slice's scope, but the screenshots therefore show a port label that is not runtime truth. Claimed failure mode: a reviewer reading the screenshot could believe the evidence hit :8004 (the default deployment port) instead of the fresh branch coordinator.

The spec header states that testid ifc-runtime-state 'does not exist on this branch', but RealIfcConsolePage.tsx:191 renders it; consequently the spec never asserts 'runtime: dev_routes_disabled' (only this run's post-hoc trace grep shows it and confirms storage_empty is absent). Claimed failure mode: a regression flipping the runtime line back to storage_empty would not be caught by the E2E.

No button was clicked: after the 404 notice, clicking 'Refresh ./storage IFC list' (enabled) re-calls /api/dev/ifc-sources; the code path sets devRoutesDisabled again on 404, but this was not observed in the browser. Claimed failure mode: refresh could transiently clear the notice or re-enable the register button between the two fetch states.
